steps.note: One step, producing a Draft. No tax is deducted without an approved configuration in force — a configuration in draft or awaiting approval deducts nothing (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A rate outside a sensible range and no fee type selected are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.

operations.name: fee.tax.config.create
operations.idempotencyKey: effective_from + tax_year + branch_id, since one configuration version takes effect per date
operations.purpose: Create a draft withholding tax configuration with every parameter the law requires.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.notes: The percentage deducted. Between 0 and 100 (E3). Configurable because the legal position has changed over the years (BR-1) — never carried forward from the previous configuration without the actor saying so.

parameters.name: annual_threshold
parameters.notes: The household's fees for the tax year above which tax applies. Assessed on the household across the year, not per invoice and not per student (BR-4).

parameters.name: fee_type_ids
parameters.notes: Which fee types count towards the threshold and are taxed. Not every charge a school raises is a fee for this purpose (BR-5, E4).

parameters.name: basis
parameters.notes: Whether the tax is calculated on the gross fee or after a concession. The two differ materially for a family holding a large reduction (BR-6), so it is never assumed.

parameters.name: tax_year
parameters.notes: The year the threshold is assessed across, as the tax authority sets it.

parameters.name: effective_from
parameters.notes: When the configuration takes effect. It does not recalculate invoices already issued (BR-8).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: configuration_id
fields.description: The configuration.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Draft. It deducts nothing (BR-2).

fields.name: version
fields.description: Incremented from any earlier approved configuration.

fields.name: rate
fields.description: The percentage.

fields.name: annual_threshold
fields.description: The household figure.

fields.name: basis
fields.description: Gross fee or After concession (BR-6).

fields.name: fee_types_counted
fields.description: Which charges count and are taxed (BR-5).

fields.name: households_above_threshold
fields.description: How many households would already be over it, so the effect is visible before it is agreed.

fields.name: supersedes_version
fields.description: The configuration this would close.

errors.meaning: The rate is outside a sensible range.
errors.note: Message: "Enter a rate between 0 and 100 percent."

errors.meaning: No fee type was selected as counting.
errors.note: Not every charge a school raises is a fee for this purpose (BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Never supply the rate, the threshold or the tax year. Every parameter is configurable because the legal position has changed over the years (BR-1), and a figure a planner carried forward from last year is a legal position nobody checked.
Never assume the basis. Gross fee and After concession differ materially for a family holding a large reduction (BR-6), and choosing one silently changes what every such household is deducted.

Never widen the fee types counted. Not every charge a school raises is a fee for this purpose (BR-5), and counting transport or examination towards the threshold pushes households over it that should not be.
Report how many households are already above the threshold. It makes the effect concrete before the configuration is agreed, and BR-4 means it is a household figure rather than a per-student one.
Never describe a draft as in force. No tax is deducted without an approved configuration (BR-2), and a school that thinks it is deducting is not.
Never chain the approval. A setting with legal consequence is not one person's decision (BR-9).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A draft is not deleted — the lifecycle runs Draft, Awaiting approval, Approved, Returned, Superseded. An unwanted draft is simply not submitted, and a configuration that changes is superseded by a new version with its own effective date (BR-8).

request.text: withholding tax ki configuration daal do — 5%, threshold 200,000, sirf tuition, gross par
request.gloss: enter the withholding tax configuration — 5%, threshold 200,000, tuition only, on the gross

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, tax year 2026-27.

steps.note: Every parameter comes from the request — none is carried forward from an earlier configuration (PR-1, PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A Draft. Nothing is deducted until it is approved (BR-2). Report how many households are already above PKR 200,000 for the year — that is who will start being deducted.

request.text: tax ka rate 4% ho gaya hai, nayi configuration banao
request.gloss: the tax rate has become 4%, build a new configuration

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, with only the rate stated.

steps.note: No plan is emitted: the threshold, the fee types, the basis and the effective date are all required and none is carried forward from the current configuration (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is created. Report what the current configuration holds and ask which parameters change with the rate — a new version restates all of them, and assuming the rest are unchanged is assuming a legal position.

request.text: configuration banao, tax har cheez par lagega
request.gloss: build the configuration, tax applies to everything

steps.note: "Everything" is passed as stated, not narrowed — but PR-3 says to check it first.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report which fee types that covers before emitting. Counting transport and examination towards the threshold pushes households over it that tuition alone would not (BR-5), and "everything" is rarely what the law means.

intent.name: fee.tax.config.approve
intent.summary: Approve a withholding tax configuration so deductions begin from its effective date. School Admin or Principal, one step.

routesHere.text: nayi tax setting manzoor kar do

routesHere: sign off the withholding tax rate Accounts entered

request.text: purane invoice pe bhi tax lagao
request.gloss: apply the tax to earlier invoices too

routesElsewhere.note: A change takes effect from its own date and does not recalculate invoices already issued (BR-8).

steps.note: One step. From the effective date, tax is deducted automatically as invoices are raised against households that have crossed the threshold (BR-3, BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the acting user entered the configuration themselves is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the approval, the status change and the audit entry together or not at all. From the effective date the amount deducted is held in its own ledger account as money owed onward — never school income and never a school expense, because the school is collecting on somebody else's behalf (BR-7). It does not recalculate invoices already issued (BR-8). Any earlier configuration is superseded.

operations.name: fee.tax.config.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: configuration_id, since a configuration carries one approval
operations.purpose: Approve a tax configuration, bringing it into force from its effective date.

parameters.name: configuration_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with version, rate, threshold, status and effective date.

parameters.notes: The tax configuration, resolved from how the actor named it — the version, or simply the current one.

fields.name: rate

fields.name: annual_threshold
fields.description: The household figure now assessed against.

fields.name: basis
fields.description: Gross fee or After concession (BR-6).

fields.name: effective_from
fields.description: When deductions begin.

fields.name: approved_by

fields.name: superseded_version

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to approve their own configuration.
errors.note: A setting with legal consequence is not one person's decision (BR-9).

planningRules.rule: Never approve a configuration the acting user entered. E5 is BR-9 working — a setting with legal consequence is not one person's decision.

Report how many households will be deducted from. The threshold is assessed on the household across the tax year (BR-4), so a family with three children reaches it where one child would not — and the number makes that concrete.

Report that the deduction is held, not earned. It sits in its own ledger account as money owed onward, never school income and never an expense (BR-7), and describing it as income misstates the school's position.
Never offer to apply the configuration to earlier invoices. It takes effect from its own date and does not recalculate what has been issued (BR-8).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An approved configuration is not withdrawn. It is superseded by a new version with its own effective date, and the earlier one is kept so a deduction made under it stays explicable. Deductions already made are adjusted only where the underlying invoice is cancelled or credited (BR-13). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, on a 5% / 200,000 configuration effective 01-07-2026.
resolvedPlans.outcome: In force from 01-07-2026. Report how many households are already above the threshold — they will be deducted from on their next invoice. The amount goes to the holding account as money owed onward, not to income (PR-3).

steps.note: In practice approve is absent from an Accounts allow-list. The API returns CANNOT_APPROVE_OWN (E5).

steps.note: Only the approval is planned. Recalculating issued invoices is not offered (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The configuration is in force from its effective date. Report plainly that invoices already issued are not recalculated (BR-8) — where a specific one was wrong, that is a cancellation or a credit with its own approval.

operations.name: fee.tax.config.return

parameters.name: configuration_id

parameters.name: branch_id

errors.meaning: The acting user entered it themselves.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. A legal setting returned without a stated objection tells Accounts nothing, and the objection is usually specific — the rate, the threshold, the basis or which fee types count.
Report what remains in force. Where no configuration has ever been approved, nothing is being deducted at all (BR-2) — which the school may not realise, and which has legal consequence.
Never adjust a parameter on the approver's behalf. Changing the rate or the basis is Accounts' work in their own session (BR-9).

reversal.statement: A return is not undone. Accounts change the configuration and submit it again, which is a fresh decision.

intent.name: fee.tax.certificate.issue
intent.summary: Issue a household its certificate of tax deducted for the year, which the parent needs to claim the amount against their own return. One step.
routesHere: issue the tax certificate for this household

routesHere.text: is family ka tax certificate jaari karo
walid ko tax katauti ka certificate chahiye
routesHere.gloss: the father needs the tax deduction certificate
produce the certificate for the year

routesHere: reissue the certificate, the invoice was credited

request.gloss: we need to deposit the tax

routesElsewhere.note: Preparing the return and recording the deposit are steps 8 of the flow; no capability is written for them. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.
The deduction is calculated from the approved configuration (BR-3). Nobody types a tax amount.
Where an invoice on which tax was deducted is credited, the deduction is adjusted and the certificate reissued (BR-13) — the credit comes first.

steps.note: One step. The figures come from the deductions actually made — nothing on the certificate is typed (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A household with no deduction for the year is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the certificate with its unique number, and the audit entry. No ledger entry is made and no money moves — the deduction happened when the invoices were raised. Where the household's position has since been corrected, the certificate is reissued with the adjusted figure (BR-13).

operations.name: fee.tax.certificate.issue
operations.idempotencyKey: family_code + tax_year, so a repeat returns the existing certificate rather than issuing a second number for the same year
operations.purpose: Issue or reissue a household's certificate of tax deducted for a tax year.

parameters.name: family_code

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with the guardian and the children.

parameters.notes: The household. The threshold and the deduction are both assessed at household level, not per student (BR-4).

parameters.name: tax_year
parameters.notes: The tax year the certificate covers.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: certificate_number
fields.description: Unique per household per tax year.

fields.name: family_code
fields.description: The household.

fields.name: fees_counted
fields.description: The household's counted fees for the year (BR-5).

fields.name: tax_deducted
fields.description: What was actually deducted. Never typed (BR-3).

fields.name: deductions
fields.description: Invoice by invoice, so the parent can reconcile it.

fields.name: reissued
fields.description: True where a correction has changed the figure since a certificate was last issued (BR-13).

fields.name: previous_certificate_number
fields.description: Superseded by this one, where reissued.

errors.meaning: No tax has been deducted from this household this year.
errors.note: Message: "No tax has been deducted from this household this year." Either they did not cross the threshold, or no configuration was in force.

planningRules.rule: Never type a figure onto a certificate. Every amount comes from the deductions actually made (BR-3), and the parent uses it to claim against their own return — a wrong figure is a wrong tax claim.
Issue against the household, never the student. The threshold and the deduction are both household figures (BR-4), and a certificate per child would understate what the family may claim.

Never treat NO_DEDUCTION as a failure to work around. It means the household did not cross the threshold, or no configuration was in force — both are answers, and the second is worth escalating (BR-2).
Report a reissue as a reissue. Where a correction has changed the figure, the certificate supersedes an earlier one (BR-13), and a parent holding the old one needs telling.
Never describe the deduction as school income. It is held as money owed onward (BR-7), and the certificate exists so the parent can reclaim it (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A certificate is not withdrawn. Where the household's position changes, a fresh certificate is issued that supersedes it (BR-13), and both stay on the record. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, after a credit adjusted the household's position.

steps.note: The same call. The API reissues with the adjusted figure and supersedes the previous number (BR-13).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A new certificate superseding the old one. Report it as a reissue and name the previous number — the parent may already have filed with it (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on a household that never crossed the threshold.

steps.note: Emitted unchanged. The API returns NO_DEDUCTION (E9).

resolvedPlans.outcome: No certificate. Report that the household did not cross the threshold this year, so nothing was deducted and there is nothing to certify — and check that a configuration is actually in force, because the other reason for a nil deduction is that none is (PR-3).
